text:
maria: FYI ran a focused profile on prefix caching after the kernel-selection change. hit-rate tanked for short prompts after the rollout.

aj: ugh, numbers?

maria: baseline (before change) prefix-hit = 82%, p50 gen latency = 45ms. after change: prefix-hit = 23%, p50 = 118ms, p95 = 410ms for the same small prompt workload.

siva: that’s huge. did the keying change? we switched some normalization in the serving runtime last week.

maria: yes — kernel selector now appends a model-variant tag into the cache-key to avoid mixing quantized kernels. looks like the tag is unique per allocation and includes a transient allocator id. cache keys ended up different across requests.

jen: oh no, allocator id should never be part of the key. that explains misses. can we strip it out at key-gen?

aj: short-term mitigation: SDK can send an explicit opt-in header so older clients reuse the old keying. Suggest header: `X-RW-Cache: allow`. Also add `Cache-Control: rw-prefetch=1` for warmup paths.

maria: tested patch to remove allocator id from key-gen locally — hit-rate jumped back to 79%. pushing a fix to canary now.

perf-bot: build/serve-canary-1765432142 deployed to canary cluster (sha: 9f3a2b).

aj: good. we should also harden client-side controls. current SDK has `cache: true/false` only. need more granular flags: `cache: {mode: \"opt-in\", includeHeaders: [\"X-RW-Cache\"]}` and `cacheKeyNormalization: \"trim-and-lower\"`.

maria: agree. also found streaming edge-case: when streaming disconnects + reconnects, SDK adds `X-RW-Stream-Session` to headers; that was being included in the key and caused misses mid-stream, creating repeated generation and extra cost.

siva: fix: server should ignore ephemeral headers when computing key. clients should avoid adding session ids to canonicalized request. document header whitelist.

jen: can we do a quick smoke for warmup strategy? idea: async prefetch route `POST /v1/prefetch` that takes a small prompt set, returns immediately and warms prefix cache across pool. header: `X-RW-Warmup: true`.

maria: benchmarked prefetch 100 unique prompts across pool: warm CPU/GPU steady-state achieved in ~18s and hit-rate for following traffic rose to 68% (vs 23% without warmup). good win.

aj: rolling plan: 1) revert allocator id change in canary (maria) 2) server: exclude ephemeral headers + stable variant tag (siva) 3) SDK: add opt-in header + cache controls + streaming session filter (jen) 4) add prefetch endpoint + docs (product + eng) 5) add regression alert rule in console: prefix-hit drop > 10% -> pager.

maria: added a short profiling log snippet below for the regression case if anyone wants to look: 

```
# before
prefix_hit: 0.82
p50_ms: 45
p95_ms: 120
# after (regressed)
prefix_hit: 0.23
p50_ms: 118
p95_ms: 410
profile: kernel_selector: alloc_tag_in_key=true -> key_entropy +1.7
```

jen: will add SDK PR with header + normalization tomorrow morning. keeping it opt-in until we stabilize.

siva: I'll patch server key-gen to sanitize tags and add a header whitelist. will monitor canary.

maria: thanks all. tagging @deploy-bot to coordinate canary -> prod if metrics look good. :eyes:
